Preface to Peasantry, by Arthur F. Raper, Chapel Hill, The University of N. Ca¬
rolina Press, 1936
\p\A study of Greene and Macon County made over a period of 7 years, in these two
representative rural Black Belt Counties, to determine the meaning of the
various New Deal activities to the population groups there.\:p\
\p\Foreword by Will. E. Alexander\:p\
\p\Zitate aus dem Vorwort:\:p\
\p\"The decadence of this (cotton-)civilization is fare advanced. The fertility of
much of the soil has been mined away... Poverty, illiteracy, undernurishment hand[sic]
handicap most of those who remain.. The decadence of this once prosperous and
influential section was not inevitable... The situation is due in part to the
misuse of the land... Cotton culture not only has destroyed the soil, but also has
resulted in the neglect of a large portion of the population.\:p\
\p\(About colored and poor white): No way has ever been found to keep a man in a
ditch without someone' staying down there with him.\:p\
\p\..To restore the land and rehabilitate the people will require a new leadership
with intelligence enough to understand that the maintenance of a decent
civilization in the South depends more upon the constructive use of the soil
than upon the "maintenance of white supremacy" – the imaginary task that has
preoccupied so much of the political leadership of this section...\:p\
\p\...It must change fundamentally the relation of the majority of the people
to the land, by affording an opportunity for ownership of the land to the
man \g\who works it\:g\. Jt must substitute for cotton a program of general
farming... These things accomplished, many of the rural South's disinherited
people may be rehabilitated into useful and intelligent citizens – an end
which never can be attained under the cotton tenancy system that has
prevailed in the past."\:p\ [space]
\p\Jn Part Four: Population Movements: farm\:p\
\p\"The Greene County 'Exodus' "– Hundreds of families moved out of Greene County
in 1922, a large number left in 1923, and still more in 1924 and 1925
when the "exodus" reached its zenith even in the late twenties families
were still boarding trains, hoping to find in Atlanta, Birmingham, Chicago
or Detroid some ready money with which to buy food and clothing.\:p\
\p\[?] .. Migration was greatest from the old plantation area and least
from the white land section in the southeastern part of the County characterized
by small holdings.. The people.. were \g\fleeing from\:g\ something
rather than being \g\attracted to\:g\ something.\:p\
\p\Zwischen 1920 und 1930 verliessen 33,5% der Bevoelkerung Greene County!\:p\
\p\Abnahme der weissen Bevoelkerung 23%, der Neger 43 %.\:p\ [space]
\p\Part Five: The New Deal:\:p\
\p\Loans for Farm and Home-National Recovery Act – Agricultural Adjustment Act –
RELIEF PROGRAM: The County poor fund, the Federal Emergency Relief Administration,
Work Relief Projects.\:p\
\p\Governor Talmadges' Program: Advertised throughout the Nation for his use of
troops in the textile strike of 1934, for his attacks on the New Deal, .. and for
his advocacy of low taxes, the present governor of Georgia is far from unpopular..\:p\
\p\(Cheap automobile tags – $ 3.-)\:p\
\p\Er war fuer niedrige Unterstuetzung, damit relief nicht mit den existierenden
niedrigen Loehnen konkurriert. Typische state-Politik! – Laesst dem Lohn-Bezieher
keine Wahl, – er muss die auf Arbeitslosen-Niveau basierten Loehne akzeptieren.
Federal programs hingegen geben direkte Unterstuetzung, teils durch \g\loans\:g\ –
(Anleihen) fuer die Saat. oder – [D]urch "Production Credit Association Loans –"
Darlehen, durch die der Farmer Mitglied dieser lokalen Associations wird, und
sein Darlehen zur Erntezeit nebst 5% Zinsen zurueckzahlt [add inline: – schlechte Wirkung:]
Viel Land verloren, indem es in den Besitz von "loan companies" ueberging.
[add inline: Am meisten Land besassen versch. Versicherungs-Gesellschaften.]\:p\
– 2 – (Forts. Preface to Peasantry)
\p\1932 kam das New Deal, – als die Baumwolle noch 5 und 6 Cents einbrachte (pro Ballen
?) (oder pro Pfund?)\:p\
\p\Many well informed people in each county.. stated unhesitatingly that there woulda[sic]
have been a great deal of suffering and that the majority of large ownership
of the large owners ... would have gone into bankruptcy before the fall of 1934,
except for the money of the plow-up, the land rented to the government, the
ten-cent and twelve-cent cotton of 1933 and 1934 43w respectively, the money
from the relief-program, and the loans from the through the Federal Land Bank,
the Land Bank Commission, and the Home Owners Loan Corporatien. \:p\ [Durchstreichung geht über in typografische Absetzung zum nächsten Absatz] [space]
\p\Wirkung der NRA im Sueden:\:p\
\p\The Negroes usually referred to the letters as meaning "Negro Removal Act",
Negro Rarely Allowed",.. while white men have been heard to call it
the "Negro Relief Act" and even "No Roosevelt Again".\:p\
\p\Die NRA brachte Vorschlaege fuer hoehere Loehne und kuerzere Arbeitszeit in inde[sic]
industriellen und kommerziellen Unternehmungen. Da circa 3/4 der Bevoelkerung
in Greene und Macon County in der Landwirtschaft oder Haushalt beschaeftigt
waren (1930 – aber allg. gueltig) wurden nur 1/4 von der NRA betroffen.\:p\
\p\Diese waren meistens Arbeiter in Cotton mills, sawmills, planing miles, oil mills,
railroad, and a fertilizer factory.\:p\
\p\The employees in some lumber camp and other places complained that under the
NRA they worked 3 or 4 hors[sic] a day, instead of twelve as formerly, and that they
had to do practically the same amount of work.\:p\
\p\Die NRA-Bestimmungen belasteten den kleinen Unternehmer mehr als den grossen,
weil sie die Produktionskosten einer weniger mechanisierten, mehr von der
Arbeit der "Haende" abhaengenden Betriebe relativ mehr verteuerten als die
der grossen Fabriken.\:p\
\p\20 in einer Greenboro Cotton Mill beschaeftigte Neger erhielten durch NRA
hoehere Loehne und arbeiteten kuerzer, – aber sie waren die ersten, die entlassen
wurden, als neue Maschinen einige Arbeiter ersoarten[sic].\:p\
